text:
The Indian equity market closed the week on a strong note, with the Nifty 50 up 8.58% to 25,030.35 and the Bank Nifty rising 8.04% to 59,086.0. Broad‑based buying was evident – the breadth score was 67.3, classified as “HEALTHY”, with 71.2% of stocks above their 20‑day moving average. Financial Services, Consumption and Infrastructure led the sector quadrants, while IT, Bank and Pharma showed weakening momentum. Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) continued their buying streak, netting INR 45,960 crore over eight sessions, whereas Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) sold INR 24,197 crore for the sixth straight session.

In IPO activity, five listings were completed last week. BLS Polymers debuted at INR 150 and closed 57.2% above issue price, the biggest first‑day jump. SFC Environmental (₹330) and Bombay Coated & Special Steels (₹82) also closed well above issue, up 25.2% and 9.8% respectively. M.K. Sons Fine Jewels (₹162) slipped 2.4% after an initial 5.6% rise, while EAAA India Alternatives (₹1,665) edged up 1.0% after a modest 0.6% opening gain. No new IPOs are scheduled for the coming week.

Looking ahead, the market may react to several cues. The India VIX, a volatility gauge, rose 14.15% to 17.47, suggesting higher short‑term uncertainty. Global cues include a 2.26% fall in the S&P 500 futures and a 4.36% decline in Nasdaq 100 futures, while Brent crude dropped 16.98% to $97.66, potentially easing inflation pressure. Domestically, a weaker USD‑INR at 93.89 (down 1.32%) could support export‑linked stocks. Keep an eye on the 20‑day moving‑average support around 24,800 for the Nifty and any policy signals that could affect the leading financial and consumption sectors.
